title.narrative: Rwanda Public Finance Management Reform Project

description.narrative: The development objective of Public Finance Management Reform Project for Rwanda is to improve budget reliability and control of funds for service delivery, enhance budget transparency and increase professionalization of the public finance officials. This project has four component. 1) The first component, Public Financial Management (PFM) IT Systems Roll Out, aims to help stabilize the systems, expand their functionality and support roll out of Financial Management Information System (FMIS) to service delivery units by enhancing functionality and stability of the FMIS. 2) The second component, Accounting and financial reporting, aims to finance activities related to the initial stage of implementation of public sector accounting reforms. 3) The third component, Performance-Based Budgeting and Medium-term Budgeting, aims to help the Government of Rwanda (GoR) strengthen its multi-year perspective of the budgeting and support implementation of performance-based budgeting methodology, including strengthening of the links between budgeting and sector strategic plans, in three line ministries. 4) The fourth component, Professionalization of PFM Staff – PFM Capacity Development, aims to fund a mass scale professionalization program for the public finance officials in the areas of accounting and audit, budgeting, procurement.
To improve budget reliability and control of funds for service delivery, enhance budget transparency and increase professionalization of the public finance officials.

title.narrative: Share of districts expenditure arrears to consolidated district budget

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. District expenditure arrears fell to 1.12 percent from a baseline of 10 percent, surpassing the target of 6 percent. This achievement was facilitated by the expansion and upgrade of IFMIS, which doubled in functionality and introduced new modules, enhancing the control of public resources. This includes project management, audit management and SDMS modules.

Target exceeded. For FY2023/24, the total aggregate expenditure outturn was reported at 101.6 percent, an improvement over the prior year's 103 percent, surpassing the target of total deviation below 5 percent. This showcases an improved adherence to the budget and indicates enhanced fiscal discipline.
Note: This indicator measures the aggregate expenditure outturn against the approved budget according to PEFA (PI-1). This approach aligns with the technical support provided under the project to strengthen the overall medium-term fiscal framework and PBB for all budget agencies.

title.narrative: Number of public finance staff that have completed a professional qualification

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. 1,085 PFM professionals were trained and attained full qualification compared to an end target of 826 and baseline of 665 individuals.

title.narrative: Share of districts expenditure arrears to consolidated district budget

comment.narrative:
The annual target has been exceeded. The expenditure arrears still remain below target at 1.12%. Only outstanding payables of RWF 9.9 billion out of RWF 881 billion of budget were waiting for payment in Local Governments as at June 30, 2024.
Source - Consolidated financial statement

Starting Y4 (FY 22/23);measurement of budget reliability has been revised to focus on the overall budget performance as opposed to the performance of few ministries (as previously measured). This indicator measures the aggregate expenditure outturn, measuring the outturn of expenditure against original approved budget as done under PEFA assessment (PI-1). This approach aligns better with the technical support provided under the project to strengthen the overall medium- term fiscal framework and the performance-based budgeting for all budget agencies. Updated result has been shared for FY 22/23, indicating overall aggregate budget outturn as 101.6%. For FY 23/24, total aggregate expenditure outturn is 100.6%.
Source - MINECOFIN Budget department

title.narrative: Improved budget transparency and citizens engagement

baseline.value: Citizens budget does not contain links between financing and results, does not incorporate citizens' feedback and published in most of the years

target.value: Citizens' budget is published annually and includes information on budget execution, the medium-term financial program, analysis of links between financing and results, and citizens feedback on programs along with suggested actions to address citizens feedback.

comment.narrative: Target partially achieved. MINECOFIN conducted a citizen engagement process during budget preparation and dissemination. Through the creation and distribution of citizen guide booklets, GoR provided feedback and insights on resource generation and the distribution of priorities. The project successfully achieved its goal regarding the annual publication of the citizen's budget on MINECOFIN's website. However, the objective of improving budget transparency through IPSAS-compliant financial statement disclosures was only partially met due to incomplete implementation of IPSAS accrual.

actual.value: Citizen budget is published annually and includes information on budget execution, the medium term financial program, analysis of links between financing and results, and incorporates citizen feedback.

comment.narrative: Target achieved. By December 2024, IFMIS capabilities were enhanced to capture non-financial performance data of PBB programs, including output indicators, baselines, quarterly targets, achievements, and narrative comments. Performance budgeting, initially piloted in four ministries and four districts expanded to all sectors under NST-2, with performance indicators included as Annex 10 in the budget estimates.

title.narrative: Representation of Female staff in Professional PFM training

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. The percentage of total female population employed in public finance roles who were trained under the project was 29.6 percent , surpassing the end target of 27.9 percent.

title.narrative: Number of public finance officials who recieved training or are in training under the project

comment.narrative:
Target exceeded. By Project close, a total of 8,209 officials employed in public finance roles received training compared to the 6,000 target. The initiative expanded qualifications in PFM and related fields, enhanced PFM professionalization by supporting ICPAR, and strengthened the procurement function. Other achievements included the creation of an internship pathway for high-performing university students to enter the public sector, and the establishment of a public sector unit within ICPAR.
Note: This indicator was revised at restructuring to include staff undertaking professional courses (but not fully completed). This was in addition to those taking other project funded short training courses, workshops and/or on the job training hired by consultants under the project.

Target achieved. By December 2024, IFMIS captured 83 percent of the education sector's expenditure, excluding primary education. Of the RWF 275.1 billion spent on primary and secondary schools, TVET, and capitation grants/school feeding, RWF 228.7 billion was recorded as real expenditure in IFMIS.
Note: This indicator assessed IFMIS coverage of the percentage of school-level expenditure (as opposed to the percentage of education institutions covered by IFMIS). The 88 percent end target reflected all education expenditure except primary school. However, since restructuring, the primary school budget increased due to the inclusion of school feeding program (increasing the denominator).

title.narrative: Improved disclosures in consolidated financial statements

baseline.value: No IPSAS standards are approved and implemented

target.value: Non-audited Government Consolidated IPSAS financial statements prepared

comment.narrative: Target not achieved. The government faced challenges in fully adopting the IPSAS accrual basis for financial statements, primarily due to necessary adjustments in opening balances. Although full accrual standards adoption was delayed, the FY 2023/24 financial statements were prepared in line with the Organic Law on PFM No. 002/2022, referencing IPSAS 33, setting the stage for future compliance. The partial adoption improved reporting accuracy and transparency, enhancing oversight by institutions like the OAG and Parliament, thereby reinforcing fiscal discipline.

actual.value: Financial statement for FY 24 will not be IPSAS complaint but is prepared on accrual basis with appropriate reference to IPSAS 33 without the need of preparing an opening balance sheet at as 1st July 2023. IPSAS compliant statement expected for FY24/25.

title.narrative: Improved program/performance-based budgeting methodology in use

baseline.value: Program budgeting methodology has weaknesses in connecting financial and performance information

target.value: Program-performance budgeting is rolled out to ministries and implementation on experiences of ministries and lessons captured.

comment.narrative: Target achieved. PBB was improved to connect performance and information by program based on the lessons learned from previous years experiences. Annex 10 was introduced to the Finance Law.

actual.value: Program-performance budgeting is rolled out to all ministries and implementation on experiences of ministries and lessons captured.

comment.narrative:
IFMIS has been configured to generate Performance Based Budget (PBB) related performance monitoring reports by tagging sub programs that are implemented under the PBB pilot. IFMIS currently captures output indicator, indicator measurement unit, indicator baselines, quarterly indicator targets and achievements, quarterly performance as well as comments. These monitoring and evaluation reports (based on these defined performance indicators) are generated to monitor actual vs targets. The extent of its usage needs to expand beyond the pilot projects to strengthening the M&E of projects.
Source: MINECOFIN IFMIS department

title.narrative: Improved disclosures in consolidated financial statements

baseline.value: No IPSAS standards are approved and implemented

target.value: Non-audited Government Consolidated IPSAS financial statements prepared

comment.narrative: Full IPSAS compliant financial statement will not be achieved, FY 2024 financial statements will be prepared on accrual basis with the recognition of several assets and liabilities for the first time. IPSAS could not be adopted mainly due to the need to adjust the opening balance of assets and liabilities as of July 1, 2023. However, given that the benefits to the users of the transitional IPSAS financial statements are less than the cost, the GoR financial statements have been prepared in accordance with the Organic Law on PFM N° 002/2022, with appropriate reference to IPSAS 33, without the need for preparing an opening balance sheet as at 1st July 2023, that would involve retrospective adjustments to the opening accumulated surplus or deficit. During the FY 2024/25, GoR aims to achieve compliance with the accrual IPSAS accounting and financial reporting framework.

actual.value: Financial statement for FY 24 will not be IPSAS complaint but is prepared on accrual basis with appropriate reference to IPSAS 33 without the need of preparing an opening balance sheet at as 1st July 2023. IPSAS compliant statement expected for FY24/25.
